title: Tenant-aware sample-rate limiter and quant-basis optimizer
author: Claire Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Large multi-tenant deployments showed non-linear token cost increases when a small set of noisy tenants drove batching and cache pressure. This PR introduces a tenant-aware sample-rate limiter (a lightweight per-tenant leaky bucket + sampling controller) plus a complementary quant-basis optimizer that selects compact quant profiles based on observed sample distributions. Goals: reduce cross-tenant tail cost, limit expensive mini-bursts that break batching efficiency, and provide safe quantization defaults per-tenant without manual tuning.

What this changes (summary): Implements a tenant-weighted sampling controller that throttles sampling rate per tenant when their burstiness meaningfully reduces global batch fill probability. Adds a runtime hook to compute short-window sample statistics and feed a heuristic that picks a quantization "basis" (int8/ptq/awq-inspired profiles) tuned to the tenant's response-length distribution and generation temperature. Introduces a cost-simlation utility used by the console to surface estimated per-tenant unit economics for proposed profiles.

Design highlights: - Sampling controller lives in runtimes/scheduler and operates at request admission time; it emits metrics (tenant.sample_rate, tenant.throttle_events) and respects per-tenant SLA hints. - Quant-basis optimizer evaluates 3 lightweight profile candidates online using cached microbenchmarks and a conservative quality delta estimate; it never upgrades to a more aggressive profile without an offline eval approval. - Fallback safety: if latency or quality regressions are observed, the system reverts the tenant to the last safe profile and marks the candidate as disqualified for 24h.

Testing and rollout plan: unit + integration tests added; canary rollout to a small set of non-critical tenants for 72h with metric gates (99th p90 latency, token cost delta < 8%). Console exposes an opt-in suggestion card for tenant owners to accept or reject quant profile changes.

Rollback: switch off feature flag, drain scheduler caches, and revert tenant sample rates to per-tenant defaults.

Notes: This PR focuses on runtime heuristics and conservative defaults; a follow-up will add an A/B evaluation harness that ties application-level quality signals (from evals) into the quant acceptance decision.

files_changed: runtimes/scheduler/tenant_sampler.go: add TenantSampler (leaky bucket + adaptive rate); emits tenant.sample_rate and tenant.throttle_events metrics; respects tenant SLA hints
runtimes/scheduler/sampler_test.go: unit tests for burst detection and sampling backoff (covers edge cases with zero-latency fast paths)
optimizer/quant/basis_selector.py: new quant-basis scoring logic, candidate ranking, conservative promotion rules; comment explains safety model
optimizer/quant/profiles/*.json: add three compact profiles (int8-lite, awq-compact, ptq-safe) and metadata describing expected quality impact
console/src/components/TenantCostSuggestion.tsx: new opt-in card showing estimated per-tenant unit econ and suggested quant basis (uses simulation endpoint)
tools/costsim/simulator.go: lightweight cost simulator used by console and tests (models batching/caching impact and estimates token unit cost)
docs/runbooks/tenant-sample-quant.md: design overview, rollout checklist, observability guide, and rollback instructions
infra/flags/flags.yaml: add feature flag runtime.tenant_sample_rate_control and config knobs for beta tenants
